Name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird
Description: Weighing less than a nickel, the ruby-throated hummingbird beats its wings about fifty times a second and can hover, fly backward, and cross the entire Gulf of Mexico, some six hundred miles, without stopping. The male's throat flashes ruby only when the light catches it.
CreationReflection: The smallest bird on the continent makes the bravest journey. God delights in doing great things through small, weak creatures, including us.
Habitat: Gardens, feeders, and woodland edges across eastern North America in summer.
